Avoid sulfonylureas as first- or second-line therapy unless safer options cannot be used — higher risk of low blood sugar, cardiovascular events and death than alternatives. If a sulfonylurea must be used, short-acting glipizide is preferred over long-acting ones (glyburide, glimepiride).
Avoid chronic use unless other options do not work and a stomach-protecting medicine (PPI or misoprostol) is taken; long-term use raises risk of stomach bleeding and kidney injury.

Avoid starting aspirin for primary prevention of heart disease because of bleeding risk — but aspirin for secondary prevention (after a heart attack or stroke) is generally indicated. This app does not ask about the reason for use, so check with a pharmacist.

Avoid starting as first treatment for atrial fibrillation or blood clots when a DOAC is possible; long-term users with well-controlled INR may reasonably continue. This app does not check the reason for use or INR.
Avoid for long-term treatment of atrial fibrillation or blood clots in favour of safer anticoagulants (e.g. apixaban); may be reasonable when once-daily dosing is needed to help adherence.

Avoid scheduled use beyond 8 weeks unless for high-risk patients (e.g. chronic NSAID or steroid use), erosive esophagitis, Barrett's esophagitis, or other demonstrated need; linked to C. difficile infection, bone loss and fractures.
Avoid as first-line for atrial fibrillation or heart failure; if used, avoid doses above 0.125 mg/day — higher doses raise toxicity risk.
Avoid as first-line for atrial fibrillation unless heart failure or substantial left-ventricular thickening is present; more toxicity than alternatives.
